info.name: Scintilla
info.comment: Provides advanced text display and editing facilities.

description.p: The Scintilla class provides advanced text editing capabilities that are suitable for modifying text files of any kind, as well as simple user input features for text input boxes. The code is based on the Scintilla project at http://scintilla.org and it may be useful to study the official Scintilla documentation for further insight into its capabilities.

Releasing the right mouse button over the editor opens a context menu with Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete and Select All. Items are disabled when they cannot be used: edits require SCIF::EDIT, Cut, Copy and Delete require a selection, and Paste requires text on the clipboard. The menu is displayed with gui/menu at the pointer position, including over a transformed or scrolled host. Closing the menu with Escape or by choosing an item returns the focus to the editor, while moving the focus elsewhere closes it without doing so.

Code assistance is provided through a completion list and a call tip, which the client opens with ShowCompletions and ShowCallTip. The CompletionCallback reports the events that typically prompt them, such as typed characters and Ctrl+Space, as well as accepted and cancelled completions. Only one of the two pop-ups is open at a time. They are drawn above the content of the scene with the editor's font and colours, are positioned at the text that they refer to, and are kept within the bounds of the scene. They follow that text when the editor scrolls, and close if it scrolls out of view. Pop-ups are not transformed with a rotated or scaled host, although their position follows it. Refer to ShowCompletions for the keyboard and pointer interaction.

action.name: Clear
action.comment: Clears all content from the editor.

action.name: Clipboard
action.comment: Cut, copy and paste text through the system clipboard.

input.param: The mode that will be used to shift data between the target object and clipboard system.

description.p: The Clipboard action provides the same cut, copy and paste operations as the editor's key bindings (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Shift+Del, Ctrl+Ins and Shift+Ins). Text is exchanged as UTF-8 through the Clipboard class. The editor also binds Ctrl+L to cut the lines that the selection touches, and Ctrl+Shift+T to copy the current line.

CLIPMODE::COPY copies the selection. CLIPMODE::CUT copies the selection and deletes it, but only once the clipboard has accepted the text. Nothing is copied if the selection is empty. A rectangular selection is copied with a line ending after each row, and is pasted as a rectangle when it is pasted into a Scintilla editor in the same process.
CLIPMODE::PASTE replaces the selection with the most recent text on the clipboard, as a single undo action. Line endings are converted to the document's line ending mode.

If Flags does not include SCIF::EDIT, cut and paste are refused with ERR::ReadOnly and reported as SEF::FAIL_RO. If the clipboard cannot be read or written, the error is logged and reported as SEF::FAIL_CLIPBOARD.

result.error: The operation completed, or there was nothing to copy.
The clipboard holds no text to paste.
The resource has not been initialised

action.name: Disable
action.comment: Disables user interaction with the editor.

action.name: Draw
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

description.p: The entire content of the editor is marked for redrawing. Painting is deferred until the next cycle of message processing, after which the scene is redrawn.

action.name: Enable
action.comment: Enables user interaction with the editor.

action.name: Focus
action.comment: Moves the user focus to the Focus viewport.

action.name: Hide
action.comment: Hides a visible object from the view of the user.

action.name: Redo
action.comment: Redo the most recently undone activity.

action.name: SaveToObject
action.comment: Save content as a text stream to another object.
action.prototype: ERR acSaveToObject(*Object, OBJECTID Dest, CLASSID ClassID)

input.param: Refers to an object that will receive the encoded data.
Can refer to a derived class that should be used when encoding the data.

action.name: Show
action.comment: Makes an object visible to the user.

method.name: AddMarker
method.comment: Adds a marker to a line.
method.prototype: ERR sci::AddMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT Marker)

input.param: The index of the line.
The marker number, from 0 to 24.

description.p: A marker is a symbol that is drawn in the symbol margin beside a line, or a highlight of the line's text, as configured by DefineMarker. Markers are typically used to indicate bookmarks, breakpoints and errors. The symbol margin is enabled with Symbols. While it is hidden, a line that carries markers is highlighted with their background colour instead.

There are 25 markers, numbered from 0 to 24. A line can carry any combination of them, and adding a marker that the line already carries has no effect. A marker stays with its line as text is inserted and deleted. If the line is joined to the previous line, the markers of both lines are combined.

method.name: DefineMarker
method.comment: Defines the appearance of a marker.
method.prototype: ERR sci::DefineMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Marker, SCMK Symbol, struct RGB8 * Fore, struct RGB8 * Bkgd)

input.param: The marker number, from 0 to 24.
The symbol to draw.
The foreground colour. If NULL, the current colour is retained.
The background colour. If NULL, the current colour is retained.

description.p: This method sets the symbol and colours of a marker, which can then be added to lines with AddMarker. Lines that already carry the marker are redrawn with the new definition. Until it is defined, a marker is drawn as a circle with a black outline and a white fill.

Symbols are drawn in the symbol margin in the Bkgd colour, with the outline and any inner sign in the Fore colour. The SCMK::BACKGROUND and SCMK::UNDERLINE symbols are drawn in the text area instead, in the Bkgd colour. If the alpha component of Bkgd is less than 255, these two symbols are blended over the line, which also tints its text. Otherwise they are drawn opaquely beneath the text. The alpha components are ignored for all other symbols.

input.param: The number of the line to delete. Indexing starts from 0.

description.p: This method will delete a single line at the position indicated by the Line parameter. If no parameters are provided or the Line parameter is less than zero, the line at the current cursor position will be deleted. If the index exceeds the total number of available lines, the last available line will be targeted.

method.name: GetLine
method.comment: Copies the text content of any line to a user-supplied buffer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetLine(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, std::span<int8_t> Buffer)

input.param: The index of the line to retrieve.
The destination buffer.

description.p: This method retrieves the string for a Line at a given index. The string is copied to the supplied Buffer, which must have enough space for the line content and a terminating null byte.

method.name: GetMarkers
method.comment: Returns the markers of a line.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetMarkers(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT * Markers)

input.param: The index of the line.
The bit mask of the line's markers is returned here.

description.p: This method returns the markers that a line carries, as a bit mask in which bit N is set for marker N. For example, a result of 0x5 indicates that the line carries markers 0 and 2.

method.name: GetPos
method.comment: Returns the byte position of a given line and column number.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetPos(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT Column, INT * Pos)

input.param: Line index
Column index
The byte position is returned in this parameter.

description.p: This method converts a Line and Column index to the equivalent byte position within the text document.

method.name: GotoLine
method.comment: Moves the cursor to any line in the document.

input.param: The line index to move to.

description.p: This method moves the cursor to a given line index. If the index is greater than the total number of available lines, the cursor is moved to the last line in the document. A line index of less than zero is invalid.

method.name: HidePopups
method.comment: Closes the completion list and the call tip.

description.p: HidePopups() closes any completion list or call tip that is open. Closing a completion list is reported to the CompletionCallback as SCAC::CANCELLED.

method.name: InsertText
method.prototype: ERR sci::InsertText(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW String, INT Pos)

input.param: A text string to add.
-1 inserts at the current cursor position, -2 replaces currently selected text, zero or above inserts at the character index indicated.

description.p: Use InsertText to insert a string at any point in the document (if adding text to the end of the document, we recommend using data channels instead).

You will need to specify the character position at which the provided String should be inserted. Two special character positions are also supported as an alternative - a value of -1 inserts the text at the current cursor position and a value of -2 replaces currently selected text.

method.name: RemoveMarker
method.comment: Removes markers from one line or from the whole document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::RemoveMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT Marker)

input.param: The index of the line, or -1 for every line.
The marker number from 0 to 24, or -1 for every marker.

description.p: This method removes a marker that was added with AddMarker. A Line of -1 removes the marker from every line, and a Marker of -1 removes every marker. Removing a marker that is not present is not an error.

method.name: ReplaceLine
method.comment: Replaces a line with new text content.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ReplaceLine(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, STRVIEW String, INT Length)

input.param: Index of the line being targeted.
The new string that will replace the line.
The number of characters to replace the target with, or -1 for the entire source string.

description.p: This method will replace an entire line with a new text string. If the new string contains line feeds, then multiple lines will be inserted at the target position. It is possible to limit the number of characters inserted from the source string by setting the Length parameter. To insert all characters from the source string, set a Length of -1.

method.name: ReplaceText
method.comment: Replaces all text within an entire document or limited range.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ReplaceText(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Find, STRVIEW Replace, STF Flags, INT Start, INT End)
method.tiriPrototype: err = ReplaceText(Find:str, Replace:str, Flags:num, Start:num, End:num)

input.param: The keyword string to find.
The string that will replace the keyword.
Optional flags.
The start of the search - set to zero if covering the entire document. If -1, starts from the current cursor position.
The end of the search - set to -1 if covering the entire document.

description.p: The ReplaceText method will replace all instances of the Find string with the content of the Replace string, between a given Start and End point. The STF::CASE, STF::SCAN_SELECTION and STF::EXPRESSION are valid flag options for this method (see FindText for details).

method.name: ScrollToPoint
method.comment: Scrolls the document to a pixel position.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ScrollToPoint(OBJECTPTR Object, INT X, INT Y)

input.param: Horizontal scroll position in pixels.
Vertical scroll position in pixels.

description.p: This method scrolls the document so that the point (X, Y), measured in pixels from the top-left corner of the document, appears at the top-left corner of the View. The Page is moved to (-X, -Y) to reflect the change.
The editor scrolls vertically by whole lines, so Y is rounded to the nearest line. Both coordinates are clamped to the scrollable range of the document.

method.name: SelectRange
method.comment: Selects a range of text, can also deselect all text.
method.prototype: ERR sci::SelectRange(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Start, INT End)

input.param: The character at which the selection will start.
The character at which the selection will end. If negative, the last character in the document will be targeted.

description.p: This method will select an area of text between a start and end point, measured in characters. It can also deselect all text if no arguments are provided.

method.name: SetFont
method.comment: Changes the font that is used for text display.

input.param: The name of the new font face.

description.p: Call SetFont() to change the font face that is used for displaying text. The Face is a family name as accepted by the Face field, e.g. Source Code Pro or Clean. The current FontSize in pixels is retained.
If the new face is invalid or fails to load, the current font will remain unchanged.

result.error: The font file could not be loaded.
No matching font could be resolved.
Failed to resolve the font handle.
Failed to create a new resource

method.name: ShowCallTip
method.comment: Displays a call tip, such as a function signature, below a position in the document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ShowCallTip(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Pos, CSTRING Text, INT HighlightStart, INT HighlightEnd)

input.param: The document position that the call tip refers to, or -1 for the cursor position.
The text to display.
The byte offset within Text at which highlighting starts.
The byte offset within Text at which highlighting ends. Highlighting is disabled if this does not exceed HighlightStart.

description.p: ShowCallTip() opens a call tip that is attached to Pos. It is typically used to show the parameters of a function while the user types its arguments. Calling ShowCallTip() while a call tip is open replaces it, which is also how the highlighted parameter is updated. Showing a call tip closes the completion list.

The call tip is displayed on the line below Pos, or above it if it would otherwise extend beyond the bottom of the scene. The Text may contain multiple lines that are separated by \n. The characters \001 and \002 are drawn as up and down arrows, which a client can use to let the user cycle through overloads by clicking them. Clicks are reported to the CompletionCallback as SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK.

Typing text, moving the cursor left and right, and deleting with Backspace keep the call tip open. It is closed by other cursor movement, Escape, a click in the editor, the loss of the focus, Backspace beyond the cursor position at which it opened, or HidePopups.

method.name: ShowCompletions
method.comment: Displays a list of completion candidates for the word at the cursor.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ShowCompletions(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Length, CSTRING Candidates, SCACF Flags)

input.param: The number of bytes of the typed prefix that precede the cursor.
Completion candidates, separated by line feeds.
Optional flags.

description.p: ShowCompletions() opens the completion list below the word that is being typed, or above it if there is more room there. The Candidates are separated by line feeds and may be given in any order. They are sorted for display and duplicates are removed. The client normally calls ShowCompletions() from the CompletionCallback in response to SCAC::REQUEST or SCAC::CHAR_ADDED.

Length is the number of bytes of the word that precede the cursor and have already been typed. The candidate that begins with this prefix is selected, and the selection follows further typing. If no candidate matches the typed prefix, the list closes. Accepting a candidate replaces the prefix with it. Showing the list closes any call tip.

While the list is open, the Up and Down arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move the selection. Enter and Tab accept the selected candidate, and Escape closes the list. Tab reaches the editor only if the scene does not use it to cycle the focus, i.e. the scene has the VPF::IGNORE_TAB flag. Other cursor movement, a click in the editor and the loss of the focus also close it. Clicking a candidate selects it, double-clicking accepts it, and the mouse wheel scrolls the list. Acceptance is reported to the CompletionCallback as SCAC::SELECTED and any other closure as SCAC::CANCELLED.
Completions edit the document on the user's behalf, so they require the SCIF::EDIT flag.

input.param: The index of the line, or -1 for the line of the cursor.

description.p: This method toggles the fold that starts at a line, which hides or shows the lines within the fold. If the line does not start a fold, the innermost fold that contains it is toggled. Folding must be enabled with FoldingMarkers, and the document needs a Lexer that supports folding.

method.name: TrimWhitespace
method.comment: Strips trailing white-space from the document.

description.p: The TrimWhitespace method will remove trailing white-space from every line in the document. Both tabs and spaces are considered white-space - all other characters shall be treated as content.
The position of the cursor is reset to the left margin as a result of calling this method.

field.name: ActivePopup
field.comment: Indicates the code assistance pop-up that is open.

description.p: This read-only field reports SCPOP::COMPLETIONS while the completion list of ShowCompletions is open, SCPOP::CALL_TIP while the call tip of ShowCallTip is open, and SCPOP::NONE otherwise.

field.name: AllowTabs
field.comment: If enabled, use of the tab key produces real tabs and not spaces.

description.p: The Tab key is only received by the editor if the IGNORE_TAB flag is set on its VectorScene. Refer to Focus for details.

field.name: AutoIndent
field.comment: If TRUE, enables auto-indenting when the user presses the enter key.

field.name: BkgdColour
field.comment: Defines the background colour. Alpha blending is not supported.

description.p: The BkgdColour applies to the text area and to all lexer styles. The margins use their own colours.

field.name: CompletionCallback
field.comment: Reports the events that relate to code completion and call tips.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to provide completion candidates and call tips. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, SCAC Event, INT Position, INT Value, CSTRING Text).
The Event is one of the following:

SCAC::REQUEST and SCAC::CHAR_ADDED are reported as they occur, so the client can respond with ShowCompletions or ShowCallTip. Position is the cursor position, and for SCAC::CHAR_ADDED the Value is the Unicode code point of the character that was typed. The client usually examines the text that precedes the cursor to choose its candidates. Ctrl+Space is reported only while the editor has the SCIF::EDIT flag.

SCAC::SELECTED, SCAC::CANCELLED and SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK are reported on the next cycle of message processing, after the editor has completed the operation. For SCAC::SELECTED, the Text is the accepted candidate and Position is the start of the replaced text, and the candidate has already been inserted. For SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK, Position is the position that the call tip refers to. The Text is empty for every event other than SCAC::SELECTED.

field.name: CursorCol
field.comment: The current column of the text cursor.

description.p: The CursorCol and CursorRow fields reflect the current row and column of the user's text cursor. Use EventCallback and listen for the event SEF::CURSOR_POS to receive updates on changes to CursorCol and CursorRow.

field.name: CursorColour
field.comment: Defines the colour of the text cursor. Alpha blending is not supported.

field.name: CursorRow
field.comment: The current row of the text cursor.

description.p: The CursorCol and CursorRow fields reflect the current row and column of the user's text cursor. Use EventCallback and listen for the event SEF::CURSOR_POS to receive updates on changes to CursorCol and CursorRow.

field.name: EventCallback
field.comment: Provides callbacks for global state changes.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive event notifications. It must be set in conjunction with EventFlags so that you can select the type of notifications that will be received.
The callback function must be in the format Function(*Scintilla, INT64 EventFlag).
The EventFlag value will indicate the event that occurred. Please see the EventFlags field for a list of supported events and additional details.

field.name: EventFlags
field.comment: Specifies events that need to be reported from the Scintilla object.

description.p: To receive event notifications, set EventCallback with a function reference and the EventFlags field with a mask that indicates the events that need to be received.

field.name: Face
field.comment: The font family used for drawing and measuring document text.

description.p: Accepts a font family name supported by the vector module's GetFontHandle() function, including bitmap faces such as Clean. The default is Source Code Pro. Regular, bold, italic and bold italic styles share this family and FontSize. Set this field before or after initialisation. Changing it reloads the styles and updates layout and margins. SetFont provides the same operation. A failed resolution preserves the current face and handles.
This field and FontSize replace the former Font object field; scripts must use these fields to customise fonts.

field.name: FileDrop
field.comment: A callback for receiving drag and drop file notifications.

description.p: Set this field with a reference to a callback function to receive notifications when the user drops a file onto the Scintilla object's surface. The prototype for the callback function is ERR Function(*Scintilla, CSTRING Path)
If multiple files are dropped, the callback will be repeatedly called until all of the file paths have been reported.

field.name: Flags
field.comment: Optional flags.

field.name: Focus
field.comment: Defines the viewport that is monitored for user focus changes.

description.p: The editor has the user focus while the Focus viewport or any of its children has the focus. Keyboard input is received from the Focus viewport during that time, and the caret is shown and blinks. If not set prior to initialisation, the Viewport is used. Clicking within the editor gives the focus to one of its internal viewports, which are children of the Viewport.

Keyboard input requires a VectorScene that is linked to a Surface. The scene uses the Tab key to move the focus between keyboard subscribers unless its IGNORE_TAB flag is set, in which case the Tab key reaches the editor.

field.name: FoldingMarkers
field.comment: Enables code folding and shows the fold margin.

description.p: Set this field to true to enable code folding. Folding is computed by the active Lexer, so a document without a lexer, or with a lexer that does not support folding, has no folds. The fold margin is shown to the left of the text and marks each fold with a box that contains a plus (contracted) or minus (expanded) sign. Clicking the box of a fold toggles it. Folds can also be toggled with ToggleFold.

The lines of a contracted fold are hidden. They are shown again if the fold is expanded, if the cursor is moved into them with GotoLine or SelectRange, or if they are edited. Setting FoldingMarkers to false expands every fold.

field.name: FontSize
field.comment: The font em size in pixels.

description.p: Sets a positive integer pixel size for every text style. The default is 14 pixels. This is not a point size and is independent of display density. Bitmap faces select their nearest supported point size. Set this field before or after initialisation. Changing it reloads the font handles and updates layout and margins.

field.name: LeftMargin
field.comment: The amount of white-space at the left side of the page.

field.name: Lexer
field.comment: The lexer for document styling is defined here.

description.p: The lexer can be changed at any time. Its keyword lists and semantic style colours are refreshed immediately. Existing folds are expanded and folding remains enabled if FoldingMarkers is set. Set the lexer to zero to display plain text. ASP uses the HTML lexer with VBScript server blocks; Tiri keywords follow the parser's reserved words.

If the DETECT_LEXER flag is set, the lexer is chosen from the file name whenever a file is loaded, and this overrides any existing value. The Lexer is left unchanged if the file name does not match a known type.

field.name: LineCount
field.comment: The total number of lines in the document.

field.name: LineHighlight
field.comment: The colour to use when highlighting the line that contains the user's cursor.

field.name: LineNumbers
field.comment: Line numbers will appear on the left when this value is TRUE.

field.name: MarginClick
field.comment: A callback for receiving clicks in the symbol and fold margins.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive notifications when the user clicks in the symbol margin or the fold margin. This is typically used to toggle breakpoints or bookmarks with AddMarker and RemoveMarker. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, SCMG Margin, INT Line, KQ Qualifiers).

The Margin is SCMG::SYMBOLS or SCMG::FOLDING, and the Line is the index of the line that was clicked. The Qualifiers indicate the modifier keys that were held, as a combination of KQ::SHIFT, KQ::CTRL and KQ::ALT. Modifier keys are only known while the editor has the user focus.

A click in the fold margin has already toggled the fold of the line (if it is a fold header) when the callback is made. While MarginClick is defined, a click in the symbol margin is reported instead of selecting the line. Clicks in the line number margin always select the line and are not reported.

field.name: Modified
field.comment: Returns true if the document has been modified and not saved.

description.p: The Modified field controls the modification state of the document. It is automatically changed to a value of TRUE when the user edits the document. To receive notification of changes to the document state, you should subscribe to the Modified field.
It is recommended that you manually set this field to false if the document is saved to disk. The Scintilla class will not make this change for you automatically.

field.name: Origin
field.comment: Sets the Path field without loading the document.

description.p: Setting the Origin will update Path without updating the content of the Scintilla object. Use for situations such as changing the document location or name.

field.name: Page
field.comment: An internally created viewport that represents the extent of the document.

description.p: The Page is created on initialisation as a child of the View. It represents the virtual extent of the document, and scrolling is achieved by moving the Page within the View. The Page can be referenced as the page of a scrollbar.

The editor manages the size of the Page. Its height allows the last line of the document to be scrolled to the bottom of the View, and its width allows the longest line to be scrolled into view. If the Page is moved by a third party, the editor scrolls to match and then snaps the Page to the nearest whole line.

field.name: Path
field.comment: Identifies the location of a text file to load.

description.p: To load data from a text file into a scintilla object, set the Path field.

If the Path is set after initialisation, the existing content will be cleared and data loaded from the location that you specify. To change the path without automatically loading from the source file, set the Origin field instead.

field.name: RightMargin
field.comment: Defines the amount of white-space at the right side of the page.

field.name: SelectBkgd
field.comment: Defines the background colour of selected text. Supports alpha blending.

field.name: SelectFore
field.comment: Defines the colour of selected text. Supports alpha blending.

field.name: ShowWhitespace
field.comment: White-space characters will be visible to the user when this field is TRUE.

field.name: String
field.comment: Manages the text data as a complete string.

description.p: A Scintilla document can be completely updated by setting the String field. Equally, the entire document can be retrieved by getting the String field. Please be aware that retrieving the document in string format can be very inefficient, as the document text is normally stored on a per-line basis. Consider using the GetLine method as the preferred alternative, as it is much more efficient with memory usage.

field.name: Symbols
field.comment: Shows the symbol margin, in which markers are displayed.

description.p: Set this field to true to show the symbol margin to the left of the text. The margin displays the markers that are added to lines with AddMarker. While the margin is hidden, a line that carries markers is highlighted with their background colour instead. Markers that highlight the text itself, such as SCMK::BACKGROUND, are displayed regardless of this setting.
If MarginClick is defined, clicks in the symbol margin are reported to it. Otherwise a click in the margin selects the line, as it does in the line number margin.

field.name: TabWidth
field.comment: The width of tab stops in the document, measured as fixed-width characters.

field.name: TextColour
field.comment: Defines the default colour of foreground text. Alpha blending is not supported.

description.p: TextColour applies to plain text, identifiers and any unclassified styles. Configure lexer and margin colours through ThemeXML. Theme colours are stored independently for each editor and are retained across lexer changes.
The defaults are a white background, black text and operators, grey comments, firebrick keywords, dark red strings, blue numbers, green directives and violet types.

field.name: ThemeXML
field.comment: Applies colours from a preconfigured XML object. This field is write-only.

description.p: Assign an initialised XML object containing one theme element with one palette child. The palette's attributes specify SVG colour strings:
description.pre: <theme> <palette background="#232a37" text="white" keyword="#70b8ff" comment="#99aabb" string="#b5d99c" number="#d4a5ff" operator="white" preprocessor="#b5d99c" type="#ffc080" error="#ff8899" margin="#99aabb" marginBackground="#303745" cursor="white" lineHighlight="transparent" selectionForeground="white" selectionBackground="#335588"/> </theme>
description.p: The theme element accepts no attributes, and the palette accepts no child elements or non-whitespace text. All palette attributes are optional and case-sensitive. Omitted colours retain their current values. Hex colours, SVG colour names and colour functions such as rgb() and oklch() are accepted. Gradients, painter lists and unknown attributes are rejected. Alpha is ignored except for lineHighlight and selection colours, where zero disables the corresponding highlight or selection override. Other alpha values currently produce opaque colours.

The colours are copied during assignment and the XML object is not retained or modified. Assigning before initialisation configures the initial colours; assigning afterwards repaints without changing text, selection or contracted folds. Invalid themes leave all colours unchanged.

field.name: View
field.comment: An internally created viewport that clips the visible content of the editor.

description.p: The View is created on initialisation as a child of the Viewport, and covers its entire area. It represents the visible window into the document and clips the Page. The View can be referenced as the view of a scrollbar, which may reduce the size of the View by changing its XOffset and YOffset values.

field.name: Viewport
field.comment: The viewport that will host the editor.

description.p: This compulsory field refers to the VectorViewport that will host the editor's graphics. If not set prior to initialisation, the Scintilla object's owner will be used if it is a VectorViewport.

field.name: Wordwrap
field.comment: Enables automatic word wrapping when TRUE.

constants.const: If there is only one candidate, it is inserted immediately and no list is shown.
Accepting a candidate also replaces the word characters that follow the cursor.
Candidates are matched to the typed prefix without regard to case.
Automatic lexer detection will occur on initialisation and at any time that a source file is loaded.
Read-only. This flag is set if the Scintilla object has been deactivated with the Disable action.

Must be defined if the document is to be editable via user input. Without it, the user can navigate and select, but edits are refused and reported as SEF::FAIL_RO. The API can modify the document regardless.
Extends the length of the document by one blank page. This is a visual effect that only has an impact when the user scrolls to the end of the document.
